record.title: Keyed — a notch on one part over a rib on the other, so the two can only assemble one way round
record.why: Purely geometric and measured: the board's notches cut to R12.60 and the carrier's ribs run R12.70..13.10, so the board seats at one of three angular positions and at no other. It exists because the antenna feeds must land on the right LDS traces; a board fitted 40 deg out would look assembled and would not work. This is iFixit's 'three notches made for the clips that hold the tag together', repurposed.

joins.a: three 26 deg notches in a board's rim
joins.b: three matching ribs on a carrier's locating rim

dof_left: tz — the key constrains rotation, not insertion
record.adds_parts_why: this joint consumes no part; it joins two. No fastener, and deliberately so — a screw would cost 1.5-2.5 mm of a 7.98 mm budget and put metal inside Apple's Ø37.31 antenna keep-out (DECISIONS.md D13).
